newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa buys Generali's 10.8 pct Axa stake.
newsitem.headline: Axa buys Generali's 10.8 pct Axa stake.

text.p: French insurer Axa said on Friday in a statement that it had bought Italian insurer Generali's 10.8 percent stake in Axa for 285 francs per share, representing a total 5.92 billion francs.
Axa shares closed on Thursday at 285 francs. The French insurer said Generali had wanted to sell its Axa stake as it no longer considered it to be a strategic holding.
Axa exercised its pre-emptive right to buy the stock.

Axa said the sale price of 285 francs gave Generali the chance for a "significant capital gain". It said Generali had started to acquire Axa shares from 1988 at an average price of 250 francs, not considering changes in exchange rates.
"The price of 285 francs was considered attractive by Axa, given the potential worth of Axa shares linked to its prospects of profitability and growth," it said.
Earlier this year, Axa announced a restructuring as a result of which Generali transformed its indirect holding in Axa into a direct holding to make its stake more liquid.
Just last March, Axa and Generali had signed a shareholder agreement reaffirming their intention to maintain their respective holdings at their present levels.
But Generali had long been dissatisfied with its holding in Axa. Last year, it threatened to sell its stake if it was not allowed to become a more active partner.
The two groups had intended to cooperate internationally but this never materialised.
Axa said the purchase lifted the uncertainty hanging over the market and eliminated the risk of large quantities of Axa shares coming into the market and weighing on the share price.

Axa was reported to have offered to buy the Italian group's stake in July for 285 francs but at that time, Generali chairman Antoine Bernheim refused, arguing that Axa shares were capable of showing a strong increase in value.
Axa chairman Claude Bebear said then that Axa's talks with Generali had not produced "any significant collaboration" between the two of the kind sought by the Italian group.
